detailedExplanation: This topic is verified against The Tiffin Girls’ School Year 9 Biology Curriculum Outline 2026–27 and the corresponding AQA GCSE Biology 8461 content.

Plants use glucose in several ways: - respiration to transfer energy; - converted to starch for storage; - converted to cellulose for cell walls; - combined with nitrate ions to make amino acids, which are used to make proteins; - converted to lipids/oils for storage, especially in seeds.
Starch is useful for storage because it is insoluble and therefore does not strongly affect water movement by osmosis.
